newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sets talks with Congress on foreign policy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sets talks with Congress on foreign policy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his senior national security team plan a special meeting next week with influential members of Congress to discuss foreign policy and seek more bipartisan consensus, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.
The meeting is scheduled for April 16 at the presidential guest house known as Blair House, across Pennsylvania Avenue from the White House.
Facing disputes over such key issues as future ties with China and NATO expansion, Clinton has been keen for some time to discuss these matters with the lawmakers, officials said.

"The president has felt that you need to foster a spirit of bipartisanship with Congress on these issues. There is a lot of stuff on the agenda. This will give us a chance to talk about broader foreign policy objectives and key priotiries and also get input from them too," one official said.
The agenda is expected to cover European security, NATO expansion, Russia, China, the need for more foreign affairs funding, among other issues.
"It's not a decision-making meeting," the U.S. official said."What we hope will come out of it is a real sense of engagement with Congress."
